drivingQuestion: At what point in the flaying does the hide stop being a 'connection' to the flesh for purposes of impurity?
outcomeNote: A mishna: the measures are stated and the dispute over the neck-hide is recorded without decision.

segments.he: מַתְנִי׳ הַמַּפְשִׁיט בַּבְּהֵמָה וּבַחַיָּה, בַּטְּהוֹרָה וּבַטְּמֵאָה, בַּדַּקָּה וּבַגַּסָּה –
segments.en: «MISHNA:» The halakhic status of the hide of an animal after it was flayed is no longer like its flesh in terms of becoming impure and imparting impurity. Nevertheless, in the case of «one who flays» either «a domesticated animal or an undomesticated animal; a ritually pure» animal that was slaughtered properly and afterward came in contact with impurity, e.g., the one flaying it is impure, «or a ritually impure» unslaughtered carcass; «a small animal,» e.g., sheep, «or a large animal,» e.g., cattle; and even after flaying the animal’s hide is still partially attached to the flesh, the hide’s halakhic status remains that of flesh in some circumstances.

These circumstances are: If he is flaying the animal «for» the purpose of using the hide as «a carpet,» a tablecloth, or to drape over a couch, in which case he would cut the hide along the length of the animal from head to tail and then remove the hide from both sides, its halakhic status remains that of flesh until he has flayed «the measure of grasping» the hide, i.e., two handbreadths.

«And» if he is flaying the animal «for» the purpose of crafting a leather «jug,» in which case he cuts a circle near the animal’s neck and removes the hide in a downward movement, its halakhic status remains that of flesh «until he flays the» animal’s entire «breast.»

segments.he: הַמַּרְגִּיל – כּוּלּוֹ חִבּוּר לַטּוּמְאָה, לִיטַּמֵּא וּלְטַמֵּא. עוֹר שֶׁעַל הַצַּוָּאר – רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי אוֹמֵר: אֵינוֹ חִבּוּר, וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: חִבּוּר עַד שֶׁיַּפְשִׁיט אֶת כּוּלּוֹ.
segments.en: In the case of «one who» seeks to fashion a jug and begins «flaying from the legs,» until he removes the animal’s hide in «its entirety,» the entire hide is considered as having «a connection» with the flesh and its halakhic status remains that of flesh «with regard to impurity,» i.e., with regard «to becoming impure and with regard to imparting impurity.» If one removed the entire hide except for «the hide over the neck, Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri says: It is not» considered to have «a connection» to the flesh, «and the Rabbis say:» It is considered to have «a connection» to the flesh «until he removes the» animal’s «hide in its entirety,» including the neck.

moves.cueHe: המפשיט בבהמה ובחיה, בטהורה ובטמאה, בדקה ובגסה
moves.summary: opens the ruling: one flaying a domesticated or undomesticated animal, pure or impure, small or large
flaying for a carpet: connection lasts until a graspable measure, two handbreadths, has been flayed
flaying for a leather jug: connection lasts until the breast has been flayed
flaying from the legs upward: the whole hide is a connection for impurity, both to contract and to convey it
moves.about: whether the hide still lying over the neck, when all the rest has been flayed from the legs upward, counts as connected to the flesh for impurity

moves.cueHe: עור שעל הצואר – רבי יוחנן בן נורי אומר: אינו חבור
moves.summary: rules that the hide remaining over the neck is no longer a connection

moves.cueHe: וחכמים אומרים: חבור עד שיפשיט את כולו
moves.summary: rule against him: it stays a connection until the entire hide is removed

edges.cueHe: רבי יוחנן בן נורי אומר: אינו חבור, וחכמים אומרים: חבור
edges.about: whether the hide still lying over the neck, when all the rest has been flayed from the legs upward, counts as connected to the flesh for impurity
